analyst_view.overall: Early view: Napoli are 27th on three points after a 4-1 defeat in Porto, eighth in Serie A, and Massimiliano Allegri was already under pressure before that game. Club Brugge are ninth on nine points after winning 2-1 at PSV, where Yann Sommer made seven saves. Rafa Marín's red card in Porto should be served at Manchester City on matchday 5, but Napoli had a long injury list (Lobotka, Di Lorenzo, Buongiorno, Neres, De Bruyne with an ankle sprain).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean a little higher: Brugge's games have been open (4-3 at Inter, 2-3 against Villa), and Napoli conceded three in the last 20 minutes in Porto, which suggests a team that collapses when chasing.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. I lean higher: Napoli will probably have to win this home game, and with Politano and Olivera as wing-backs in their predicted line-up they should force corners from a Brugge side that won at PSV with Sommer making seven saves.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. I lean higher: a Napoli side under pressure, at home and near the elimination places, plus Marín's red in Porto, point to a tense game. The referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.2 shots. I lean lower: Napoli's injuries in midfield (Lobotka, possibly De Bruyne) take away a lot of their creativity, and Brugge are comfortable defending in a block and breaking.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.8 shots on target. I lean lower for the same reasons: Napoli's attack has been blunt beyond McTominay, and Brugge's shooting is concentrated in Tresoldi and Forbs.
